title: What If Your Skin Was Blue? One Kentucky Family's Was for 150 Years

scenes.text: What if you were born with blue skin? In one Kentucky family, it happened for generations.
Around 1820 a couple settled by a remote creek, both carrying one rare gene. Four of their seven children were blue.
Isolated in the hills, relatives married relatives, and the blue kept returning for about 150 years.
Their blood was chocolate brown. Ten to twenty percent of it was a form that can't carry oxygen. Normal is under one.
Yet they were healthy, and many lived into their eighties and nineties.
In the 1960s a doctor gave two of them a blue dye, methylene blue. Within minutes, for the first time in their lives, they were pink.

description:
What if your skin was blue? Around 1820 a couple who both carried the same rare recessive gene settled at Troublesome Creek in eastern Kentucky. Four of their seven children had blue skin, and in the isolated hills the trait kept reappearing for about 150 years.
The cause was hereditary methemoglobinemia: 10 to 20 percent of their hemoglobin was a form that cannot carry oxygen, against under 1 percent normally, turning the blood chocolate brown. In the 1960s a hematologist treated two family members with methylene blue and their skin turned pink within minutes. The last known child born blue, in 1975, lost the colour within weeks.
